house.description: Legislators clarified to be able to perform civil marriages.

House.text: Introduction and first reading, referred to Judiciary Finance and Civil Law

bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to civil marriages; clarifying that legislators may perform civil marriages; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 517.04.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 517.04, is amended to read:

517.04 PERSONS AUTHORIZED TO PERFORM CIVIL MARRIAGES.
[+(a) +]Civil marriages may be solemnized throughout the state[+ by any mode recognized in section 517.18 or+] by an individual who has attained the age of 21 years and[+ who+] is[+: +]
[+(1)+] a judge of a court of record[-,-][+ or+] a retired judge of a court of record[-,-][+; +]
[+(2)+] a court administrator[-,-][+ or+] a retired court administrator with the approval of the chief judge of the judicial district[-,-][+; +]
[+(3)+] a former court commissioner who is employed by the court system or is acting pursuant to an order of the chief judge of the commissioner's judicial district[-,-][+; +]
[+(4)+] the residential school superintendent of the Minnesota State Academy for the Deaf and the Minnesota State Academy for the Blind[-,-][+; +]
[+(5)+] a licensed or ordained minister of any religious denomination[-,-][+; +]

[+(6) a current member of the senate or the house of representatives; or +]

[+(7)+] an individual who registers as a civil marriage officiant with a local registrar in a county of this state[-, or by any mode recognized in section 517.18-].
[+(b)+] For purposes of this section, a court of record includes the Office of Administrative Hearings under section 14.48.

[+EFFECTIVE DATE.+]

[+This section is effective the day following final enactment. +]

(6) a current member of the senate or the house of representatives; or
This section is effective the day following final enactment.
